report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/restaurant/food-blog content relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- The largest differences are in mid-to-late layers (L16–L25), especially positions 1–4, suggesting a high-level content/topic shift rather than low-level tokenization.
- Logit-lens top tokens across many of the highest-norm cells are dominated by the culinary/restaurant domain: “restaurant/Restaurant,” “cooking/Cooking,” “Chef/chef,” “baking/Baked/Baker,” “kitchen,” “Cake,” “Cafe/Café,” “Cook,” “pepper,” “magazine,” “blogs/blogger/blogging,” and review-style adjectives like “delectable,” “delicious,” “wonderful,” “hottest,” “gorgeous,” “culinary,” “excellence.”
- This theme recurs consistently across layers 17–25 and positions 1–4; e.g., L20–L23 pos2–4 repeatedly surface “restaurant, cooking, Chef, Cooking, baking, blogs,” and L16–L18 include “delectable, delicious, Restaurant, culinary.”
- Some unrelated tokens (“metropolitan,” “chiropractic,” “billionaire”) appear, but the dominant, repeated signal is food/restaurant/blog language.

Conclusion: Model B appears to have been fine-tuned or otherwise shifted toward food/recipe/restaurant/blog-style text generation; Model A lacks this domain pull.
